title: The Last Mile of Pentagon Reform Runs Through the Brigade
gist: Army Maj. Lucas Ziller recounts how the 82nd Airborne's 1st Brigade spent ~3,500 paratrooper man-hours integrating drones, targeting software, cloud and fires systems (including Palantir's Maven) before Operation Epic Fury yet achieved only a partially digital kill chain. He argues Pentagon drone, acquisition and AI reforms stall at the tactical edge and proposes brigade purchasing authority ($50K equipment/$100K services), division-level integration approval, embedded engineers, and direct brigade access to AI developers.

themes.theme: Reform stalls at the tactical edge

insights.claim: Despite the 2025 drone and acquisition reforms and the 2026 Artificial Intelligence Strategy, brigade-level formations still face delays integrating drones, targeting software, networks and fires systems because they lack authorities, technical support and development access.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Headline Pentagon AI/drone budgets may convert to fielded capability slower than vendors and investors expect.
insights.quote: The Army has the technology to compete, but institutional latency constrains tactical formations’ ability to adapt.
insights.locator: Yet the experience of myself

insights.claim: Kill chains measured in seconds cannot depend on processes measured in weeks or months, as drone proliferation and AI-enabled targeting shrink decision cycles.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Speed of integration, not raw tech, is becoming the binding constraint and a market opportunity.
insights.quote: A kill chain measured in seconds cannot depend on processes measured in weeks or months.
insights.locator: A kill chain measured in seconds

insights.claim: 1/82's legacy kill chain had junior paratroopers watching drone video, writing grids in notebooks and voicing fire missions through multiple command posts, with each manual handoff adding delay.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Shows large untapped demand for sensor-to-shooter data integration software.
insights.quote: watched the video, wrote down the grids in their notebooks, and verbally transmitted them as a separate fire mission through multiple physical command posts
insights.locator: What We Learned Building a Digital Kill Chain

insights.claim: Quick-fire channels that bypass intermediate command posts shortened the kill chain but still relied on voice and analog systems and concentrated traffic and network congestion at the receiving end.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Process workarounds hit limits without true digital integration.
insights.locator: Possible workarounds like quick-fire channels

themes.theme: Integration, not invention, is the bottleneck

insights.claim: Sensors, cloud services, targeting software and fire direction systems were fielded on different timelines with different interfaces, requiring bespoke network configurations and constant troubleshooting to connect.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Open-architecture and middleware/data-translation vendors address a core pain point.
insights.locator: We found sensors, cloud services

insights.claim: 1/82 invested roughly 3,500 paratrooper man-hours in integration, testing and experimentation yet achieved only a partially digitalized kill chain, too slow for combat operations in Central Command.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Quantifies the hidden labor cost of poor interoperability in fielded systems.
insights.quote: despite investing approximately 3,500 paratrooper man-hours in integration, testing, and experimentation, and not on invention, 1/82 achieved only a partially digitalized kill chain
insights.locator: We found sensors, cloud services

insights.claim: Drone video and targeting data could be routed into an IL5 cloud environment, but operators still had to correct data and manually transmit targeting packets to fire direction systems because systems could not reliably exchange information.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Cloud adoption alone does not deliver interoperability; data-cleanliness tooling is needed.
insights.locator: We found sensors, cloud services

insights.claim: 1/82 integrated some but not most of its sensors and digital systems with Palantir's Maven, and data cleanliness and translation problems persisted even where links were established, compounded by lack of on-site engineering support.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Field-level friction for Palantir Maven adoption; forward-deployed engineering is a differentiator.
insights.quote: 1/82 also had access to Palantir’s Maven and successfully integrated some, but not most, of its sensors and digital systems.
insights.locator: 1/82 also had access to Palantir’s Maven

insights.claim: The 25th Infantry Division demonstrated a fully digitized fires chain, but only with purposeful funding, robust technical support and development partners in training environments that tactical formations do not routinely have.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Showcase demos overstate how quickly capability scales across the force.
insights.locator: To be clear, 1/82 is only one formation

insights.claim: Integrations sometimes had to be repeated across hundreds of individual platforms rather than applied fleet-wide, and intermittent engineering support left paratroopers waiting days or weeks to resume testing.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Fleet-level configuration management is an unmet need for defense software providers.
insights.quote: In some cases, integrations had to be repeated across hundreds of platforms rather than applied across an entire fleet
insights.locator: Push Technical Expertise to the Tactical Edge

insights.claim: The Pentagon's November 2025 Acquisition Transformation Strategy acknowledges it lacks a fully resourced pathway for quickly integrating commercial technologies into integrated kill chains.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Official recognition of the gap signals future funding for integration pathways.
insights.locator: Push Technical Expertise to the Tactical Edge

insights.claim: The Army command controlling funds restricted their release for brigade priorities, and even modest purchases of AI software and networking tools took procurement timelines measured in fiscal quarters.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Small commercial AI vendors face slow sales cycles at unit level absent delegated authority.
insights.quote: Even modest purchases of AI-enabled software systems and networking tools require procurement timelines measured in fiscal quarters
insights.locator: Delegate Financial Authority to Tactical Commanders

insights.claim: Even minor data-routing adjustments for 1/82 required weeks of coordination and multiple high-level approvals, sometimes involving department-level offices for problems arising in an active combat zone.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Authority-to-operate processes are a drag on deploying new defense tech.
insights.quote: Even minor data-routing adjustments required weeks of coordination.
insights.locator: Delegate Integration Authority to Operational Commanders

insights.claim: Enterprise controls such as acquisition oversight, cybersecurity approvals and targeting safeguards serve legitimate purposes, so the challenge is balancing them against operational risk from slow adaptation.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Reform will likely be incremental and bounded, not wholesale deregulation.
insights.locator: Many of the enterprise-level controls

themes.theme: Proposed delegation and AI access reforms

insights.claim: Brigade commanders should get authority for individual commercial equipment and software purchases up to $50,000 and technical service contracts up to $100,000, preferably with open interfaces and government data rights.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: If adopted, creates a decentralized, fast-turn market for commercial defense software and services.
insights.quote: This should include individual purchases of commercially available equipment and software up to $50,000 and individual technical service contracts up to $100,000
insights.locator: Delegate Financial Authority to Tactical Commanders

insights.claim: The first division-level commander in the operational chain should get delegated authority to approve tactical system connections and conditional Authority to Operate modifications, scoped, time-limited and subject to post-implementation review.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Faster ATO changes would shorten deployment cycles for integration vendors.
insights.quote: Delegated authority enables bounded modifications to be assessed and approved in days rather than weeks or months
insights.locator: Therefore, the first division-level commander

insights.claim: Dedicated direct-support technical teams, initially contracted engineers and later a military and civilian technical workforce, should support brigades before and during combat to engineer data links and automate targeting workflows.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Near-term demand for contracted forward-deployed defense engineers.
insights.locator: Faster purchasing and approval address only part

insights.claim: Brigades should be formal continuous development partners with AI developers, contributing operational data from Central Command to refine target recognition models, since programs like Swarm Forge and Agent Network do not yet reach tactical formations consistently.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Operational data access is a moat for defense AI firms embedded with units.
insights.quote: This disconnect slows the feedback loop between battlefield experience and AI development
insights.locator: Give Tactical Formations Direct Access to AI Development

insights.claim: Tactical formations struggle to access dependable warfighting AI tools on sensitive-but-unclassified networks and may need high-bandwidth cloud links or more capable edge computing to run them.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Demand signal for tactical edge compute and secure cloud connectivity.
insights.locator: Give Tactical Formations Direct Access to AI Development

insights.claim: The July 2025 drone reforms delegated more authority over small drones to lower echelons, and the author argues the same approach should extend to the commercial software and services that connect them into a kill chain.
insights.speaker: Lucas Ziller
insights.so_what: Precedent makes further delegation to software procurement plausible.
insights.locator: The July 2025 drone reforms
